## Not a lecture hall

The audience is a mix of working trainers, tactical practitioners, and training-science researchers. The point of the room is not to sit through talks. It is to put methods on the mat, in front of people who train for a living, and take them apart together.

::: {.triad}
::: {}
### Watch
Every session opens with a hands-on demonstration. Presenters run their method live, with attendees on the mat or close enough to see the details.
:::
::: {}
### Ask
Hard questions are the point. Presenters explain what they do and why, then the room pushes on the evidence, the trade-offs, and the edge cases.
:::
::: {}
### Take home
The goal for every attendee is the same: leave with something you can use in your next training cycle.
:::
:::

## How a session runs

Every session is 50 minutes, and the clock favors the mat.

::: {.format-bar}
::: {.seg-demo}
[25 min]{.seg-min} [Hands-on demonstration]{.seg-label}
:::
::: {.seg-why}
[15 min]{.seg-min} [What and why]{.seg-label}
:::
::: {.seg-qa}
[10 min]{.seg-min} [Audience input]{.seg-label}
:::
:::

[One 50-minute block, single track, no live fire. Sims, scenarios, and mat work.]{.format-caption}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
# "What attendees say" renders only when data/quotes.csv has rows.
# Add one row per quote: quote,attribution  (e.g. "Best two days of training all year","Firearms instructor, 2026")
q <- tryCatch(read.csv("data/quotes.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE),
              error = function(e) NULL)
if (!is.null(q) && nrow(q) > 0) {
  cat("## What attendees say\n\n")
  cat("::: {.quote-row}\n\n")
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(q))) {
    cat(sprintf("::: {.quote-card}\n%s\n\n[%s]{.quote-attr}\n:::\n\n",
                q$quote[i], q$attribution[i]))
  }
  cat(":::\n\n")
}
```
